# Commit Messages

Commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits 1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) specification.

## Valid Types

Use exactly these 8 types (from Angular's current commit message guidelines):

- `feat:` — new feature
- `fix:` — bug fix
- `build:` — build system changes, dependency updates, maintenance tasks
- `ci:` — CI configuration changes
- `docs:` — documentation changes
- `perf:` — performance improvements
- `refactor:` — code restructuring without behavior change
- `test:` — test additions or updates

## What NOT to Use

Do NOT use `chore:`. It comes from the defunct AngularJS 1.x convention and is not part of current Angular standards. Use `build:` instead for maintenance tasks that don't fit another type.

Do NOT use `style:`. It is absent from current Angular conventions. It persists in `@commitlint/config-conventional` out of inertia but has no authoritative backing. Use `refactor:` for whitespace and formatting changes.

## When No Type Fits

When no type fits perfectly, prefer `build:` over inventing new types or using defunct ones.

## Format

```text
<type>[optional scope]: <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```

The Conventional Commits spec mandates only `feat` and `fix` as types. The full 8-type list above follows Angular's current commit message guidelines.

## See Also

For the descriptive history of why `chore:` and `style:` are defunct, see [jewzaam/knowledgebase](https://github.com/jewzaam/knowledgebase) — `common/commit-conventions.md`.
